name: Dotted Line Face
baseMeaning: A face with a dotted line outline.
tldr: 🫥 marks a deliberate disappearance: the sender is fading out, becoming invisible, or leaving a conversation.

contextMeanings.meaning: Used as a lone reply, 🫥 says the sender has already faded and is no longer fully present.
When attached to a profile update, 🫥 can announce that the sender has erased their presence without giving the reason.
In a dating profile or soft-launch, 🫥 suggests that the sender's former identity or chapter has dissolved.
In a work channel, 🫥 can signal that someone is withdrawing from the conversation or project without a formal handoff.

platformNotes.note: On TikTok, 🫥 can close a caption or mark a profile update as the sender's disappearance from an old identity. It fits the broader use of softer exits instead of a dramatic goodbye.
In an Instagram bio, 🫥 works especially well alone or beside a city. It turns the profile into a notice that the previous version of its owner has vanished.
In iMessage, sending 🫥 as the only response says the sender has stopped being fully available. The placement carries much of the meaning.
In Slack, 🫥 can mark someone leaving a channel or project without a normal handover. Because colleagues may need practical information, add a clear update when the work actually requires one.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z users are the most likely to reach for 🫥 because younger senders have adopted the newer soft-exit vocabulary. It reads as a deliberate way to become invisible.
Millennials may recognize 🫥 and use it in casual conversations, though it is less central to their usual exit vocabulary than a wave or a direct goodbye.
Many Gen X users are less likely to recognize 🫥 because older users have picked it up less often. An unfamiliar recipient may need the accompanying sentence.

warnings.title: Unfamiliar to older recipients
warnings.description: Some older users may see only a strange blank face and miss the deliberate disappearance. Pair 🫥 with a plain statement such as “I’m stepping away for now” when clarity matters.

seoDescription: What does 🫥 mean? It signals that the sender is withdrawing, fading out, or deliberately becoming invisible in a chat or bio.

longForm.overview:
At the glyph level, 🫥 starts with a face reduced to a dotted outline. The figure is still visibly a face, but its broken contour suggests someone present in form while becoming invisible. Introduced in the early 2020s, it arrived with a small visual idea that later became useful language: being there as only an outline.

That outline now carries a clearer social meaning. Someone sends 🫥 to announce that they have already faded, stepped away, or erased their presence rather than staging a blunt goodbye. It differs from the ghost emoji’s playful “boo,” and it does not suggest that the sender is losing control the way the melting face can. 🫥 feels deliberate: I have decided to become invisible.

Its main home is the soft exit. In a bio, 🫥 can replace a detailed explanation with “new chapter.” As a lone thread reply, it says, “I am not really here anymore.” The emoji is blunt about the disappearance while still leaving the sender less exposed than a formal farewell would.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
In a thread, 🫥 often arrives as the only reply. That placement matters: the sender is not joking about the message they received; they are marking their own absence after it. A bio may contain 🫥 alone or beside a city, turning a profile update into a clean statement that the previous version of the sender has disappeared. “new chapter 🫥” works the same way in a soft-launch.

The emoji is especially useful when the sender wants to leave without either staying visibly available or writing a long explanation. It can close a conversation, step out of a group, or signal that a new place or identity has replaced the old one. Because 🫥 is precise about disappearing but vague about the reason, it often functions as the emotional part of an exit.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🫥 when the conversation still needs a clear handoff, especially at work. A coworker who sees the emoji may understand that someone is leaving but still not know which task, deadline, or channel they now own. In dating, family, or friendship conversations, it can also feel less like an exit and more like an unexplained brush-off.

Older recipients may not recognize 🫥 and may read it as an odd blank face rather than a decision to withdraw. Add a sentence when the meaning is important: “moving next week, so I’m fading out 🫥.” If you only want to end a conversation lightly, 👋 is clearer. Use 🙃, 🥱, or another playful fade only when a joke is actually wanted.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🫥, a returned 🫥 accepts the exit without demanding a long emotional discussion. For a closer relationship, a plain question such as “you okay, or just going quiet?” can turn the disappearance into an actual conversation. Keep it light if their message seems playful, but do not ignore a possible sign that they are upset.

If you sent 🫥 and the recipient follows up, decide whether you are truly withdrawing or simply wanted a dramatic goodbye. You can clarify with “I’m stepping away for now” or “that was more dramatic than I meant.” If 🫥 appears on your own content, treat it as a deliberate signal unless work or family responsibilities require you to explain what happens next.

faqs.question: What does 🫥 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: If he sends 🫥 as the only reply, he is usually saying he has faded or is no longer fully present. It does not reliably indicate romantic interest or any particular gender-specific meaning.

faqs.question: Is 🫥 flirty?
faqs.answer: Usually not. 🫥 is more often a deliberate disappearance or soft exit, including on dating profiles, than an invitation to flirt.

faqs.question: What does 🫥 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🫥 can mark a caption or profile update as the sender's exit from an old identity or chapter. It is usually about becoming invisible, not reacting to the post's subject.

faqs.question: Does 🫥 mean he is ignoring me?
faqs.answer: When 🫥 is the only response, it can mean the sender has already decided to withdraw. A direct question is still the clearest way to find out whether they are upset, busy, or ending the exchange.

conversationExamples.message: new chapter, old me is gone 🫥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is presenting the profile change as a complete break with their former identity. If you want more, ask what changed; do not assume 🫥 is a sign of continued romantic interest.

conversationExamples.message: moving next week so i'm fading out for a bit 🫥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji is adding a deliberate, slightly comic quality to a temporary withdrawal. Reply with 🫥 to match the joke or ask when they want to reconnect.
The sender is announcing a withdrawal, but the message does not provide a useful handover. Ask which tasks or deadlines remain before accepting the emoji as the entire update.
The sender wants the family chat closed without a detailed explanation. If the disappearance concerns you, check in directly; otherwise, leave them to the exit they chose.
The profile-style message uses the dotted face to say that an old version of the sender has disappeared. A friendly reply can welcome the change without demanding every detail immediately.
